note: HAND-CURATED from live-verified sources. Every url returned HTTP 200 on lastVerified date via browser UA. This is the fastest-rotting data in the app - re-verify before trusting. Dead as of 2026-08-10 and deliberately EXCLUDED: testri.org (no connection), dancesafe.org/chapters (404), NASTAD participant pages (none exist).
reality: Direct-to-individual lab checking is scarce but not zero. DrugsData paused intake in April 2024 under DEA order (no change expected before 2027); UNC's national mail-in program works through harm reduction organizations. Community-run services are emerging - Rebel Analytics in NYC advertises free testing with a mail-based expansion. For most people the practical route is still a local program: most US drug checking lives inside syringe service programs.

national.name: UNC Street Drug Analysis Lab
national.access: Ask a local syringe service program or harm reduction org to submit for you; the lab offers free kits to any US public health harm reduction organization. Free for NC organizations and drug user unions.
national.anon: The lab states it holds nothing about individuals: no names, nothing.

national.name: Rebel Analytics (Rebel Harm Reduction)
national.access: Free, community-funded testing (FTIR, immunoassay strips, reagents, lab-partner mass spec). Their site describes a mail option for people outside NYC but does not publish which states, turnaround, or intake rules - contact them before sending anything.
national.anon: Anonymity policy not published on their site - ask them directly.
national.caveat: Details verified only as far as their own pages state them, 2026-08-10.

national.name: DrugsData (Erowid)
national.access: Not accepting samples since April 2024 (DEA order); no change expected before 2027, per their homepage. The archive of past results remains searchable and useful.

national.name: NEXT Distro
national.access: Mail-based naloxone and fentanyl test strips - strips are self-testing, not lab checking. Availability varies by state law.

programs.name: MADDS / StreetCheck
programs.access: Free through partner orgs in ~19 communities; anonymous option. Accepts powders, rocks, pills, single-use pipes/cookers/cottons, baggies with residue. Not syringes or plant matter.

programs.name: NYC Health drug checking at SSPs
programs.access: Walk-in with a trained technician (FTIR + strips). Powders and pills; plant matter and most liquids cannot be tested. Call ahead to confirm.

programs.name: NYS DOH drug user health FAQ
NC Safer Syringe Initiative directory
programs.access: Drug checking reaches individuals through SSPs; the UNC lab is free in-state.

programs.name: Rapid Analysis of Drugs (RAD)
programs.access: Through Maryland SSPs only - residue swabs from used equipment, deidentified. Ask your SSP.

programs.name: Vermont community drug checking
programs.access: Legal statewide since 2023; availability varies by site - ask your syringe service program.

programs.name: WA Community Drug Checking Network
programs.access: Anonymous; drug or residue in a pipe or cooker. Not every site is listed - ask a local harm reduction agency.

programs.name: SCOPE - SF AIDS Foundation
programs.access: Free, anonymous, drop-in FTIR. 117 6th St (Mon 3-6, Tue-Wed 12-6) and 558 Clayton St (Fri 5:30-7:15). About 10-15 minutes; one sample per person per day. Call/text 415-361-8183.

programs.name: CDPH community drug checking
programs.access: Runs through partner orgs; no public site list exists. Free test strips at CDPH clinics, or email osu.cdph@cityofchicago.org.

locators.name: Harm Reduction Near You (National Harm Reduction Coalition)

legality.text: Whether test strips and checking equipment are legal depends on your state, and mailing samples touches state paraphernalia law - no program publishes a blanket promise that mailing is legal. Two maps track the actual laws:

sources.name: LAPPA state map - fentanyl test strips
Network for Public Health Law - drug checking equipment legality

grassroots.note: Peer-run and mutual-aid networks. Many operate primarily on social media - linked here as profiles, never embedded: an Instagram embed would hand Meta the IP of everyone opening this page.

orgs.name: Grassroots Harm Reduction
orgs.scope: National buyers’ club supplying local programs
orgs.access: Open to any organization or program that gives harm reduction supplies away free. Not a direct supplier to individuals — it is how the program near you affords what it hands out, and where to start if you want to run one.

orgs.name: Rebel Harm Reduction
orgs.scope: NYC community drug checking and supplies (see national list)
